decisions.reason: As a low-carrying-cost dental consumable with its own page and a clear fit to the firm's core lab workflow business, it still has option value and is unlikely to be withdrawn quickly.
This thermoforming blank is close to the firm's established materials offering, cheap to keep in the portfolio, and still early enough that management would likely preserve the option.

The lacquer appears to have a smaller initial commitment because it was only mentioned on the site, but as a low-cost adjacent material its uncertainty is not yet resolved enough to justify dropping it.
The intraoral contrast spray supports digital dentistry and was given stand-alone presentation, so its strategic fit and still-open upside argue for keeping it on the market.

The custom earmold line fits the firm's hearing-care capabilities, but because custom products tie up more operational resources than simple materials, management would keep it while watching traction closely.

Custom hearing protection earmolds are a more niche and somewhat less central extension, and with higher carrying demands plus several other innovation options, management would be more willing to reallocate resources away from it.
